intro: The Commanders beat the Giants 24-21 on Thursday night to tighten the NFC East, and the Rams lost Puka Nacua for at least five games. Sunday brings Fernando Mendoza's first start for Las Vegas and a Steelers-Bengals showdown for the AFC North lead. 160 stories across all 32 teams.

top.label: Biggest Story
top.headline: Raiders hand the offense to No. 1 pick Fernando Mendoza
top.dek: Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota for a 2027 third-round pick, then named Mendoza the starter. His first NFL start comes Sunday at home against Seattle. GM John Spytek said the rookie passed every test.

top.label: Injury Watch
top.headline: Rams place Puka Nacua on injured reserve
top.dek: Coach Sean McVay said Nacua will be out for an extended period. He cannot return before the Dec. 20 game against Dallas, so he misses the Cardinals, Packers, Chiefs and 49ers.

top.label: Player Spotlight
top.headline: Jayden Daniels drives Washington 71 yards in 49 seconds
top.dek: Daniels hit Stefon Diggs for a 32-yard touchdown late in the fourth quarter to beat the Giants 24-21. Rasul Douglas then intercepted J.J. McCarthy to seal it. The Commanders improved to 3-5-1.

top.label: Stat of the Day
top.headline: 8: sacks on Justin Herbert in the Chargers' loss to Houston
top.dek: Herbert went down a career-high eight times in the 44-22 loss to the Texans. It was the most sacks on a Chargers quarterback in a game since Dan Fouts in the 1970s. Los Angeles is the league's only winless team at 0-8.

top.label: What's Next
top.headline: Steelers visit Bengals with AFC North lead on the line
top.dek: Both teams are 6-2 and riding four-game winning streaks. Sunday Night Football kicks off at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC. A Pittsburgh win gives the Steelers the head-to-head tiebreaker after their 30-27 win in Week 3.

teams.name: Buffalo Bills
teams.headline: Bills hit 7-1, best start since 1993

stories.text: Bills reach 7-1 for the first time since 1993
stories.summary: Buffalo beat Minnesota 23-6 on Monday night and has won four straight. The defense has allowed 16 points over its last two games, after giving up 28.5 a game before the Week 7 bye. The Bills now lead the AFC East, though New England holds the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.text: Spencer Brown sits out Thursday with an ankle issue
stories.summary: The starting right tackle missed practice Thursday after a limited Wednesday. Cornerback Christian Benford (wrist), tight end Dalton Kincaid (ankle) and linemen Alec Anderson, Dion Dawkins and Connor McGovern all practiced on a limited basis. Safety Sam Franklin Jr. (shoulder) also popped up late. Game designations come after Friday's practice.

stories.text: James Cook carries it 31 times for 107 yards
stories.summary: Cook ran for 107 yards and a late touchdown against Minnesota, after just 33 yards on 15 carries at halftime. He enters Week 10 with 814 rushing yards and eight touchdowns in eight games. His 169 carries rank third in the league.

stories.text: 322: Josh Allen ties Peyton Manning for touchdowns
stories.summary: Allen has 322 regular-season touchdowns, 232 passing, 88 rushing and two receiving. That ties Manning for the most by any player in his first 10 NFL years. Tyler Bass also pushed his franchise-record field goal streak to 24.

stories.text: Bills visit the Jets on Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Buffalo goes to MetLife Stadium on a short week after Monday night. The Bills lead the league in yards per game (386.4) and points per game (32). Watch whether the banged-up offensive line holds up against a Jets pass rush led by rookie David Bailey.

teams.name: Miami Dolphins
teams.headline: McCord starts as Willis goes to IR

stories.text: Kyle McCord makes first start after Willis goes to IR
stories.summary: Malik Willis landed on injured reserve with a groin injury and will miss four games. McCord, 24, starts Sunday at Indianapolis for a 1-7 Dolphins team. Willis can return for the Dec. 13 home game against Chicago.

stories.text: Dolphins lose Willis, Sieler and center Brewer is in protocol
stories.summary: Willis is out at least four weeks. Defensive tackle Zach Sieler is done for the year with a torn biceps. Starting center Aaron Brewer is in the concussion protocol, which puts Miami's line at risk on McCord's debut. Running back De'Von Achane is also out for the season.

stories.text: Kyle McCord brings big-college numbers to the NFL
stories.summary: McCord threw for 4,779 yards at Syracuse in 2024, an ACC single-season record that also led the FBS. He will be the 29th different Dolphins starter since Dan Marino retired. Offensive coordinator Bobby Slowik expects fewer deep runs from the quarterback with Willis out.

stories.text: 46: A punter throws Miami's longest play of the day
stories.summary: In the 19-9 loss to Detroit, punter Bradley Pinion completed a 46-yard pass to running back Kaytron Allen. Detroit's Jack Fox also completed a pass, and RedZone reported it was the first game in NFL history in which both punters did.

stories.text: Dolphins visit the Colts on Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Miami is 1-7 and Indianapolis is 2-7 with five straight losses. The Colts have traded Quenton Nelson, DeForest Buckner, Keenan Allen and Josh Downs in the past two weeks. The Dolphins have run for 100 yards or more in five of their last seven games, and that run game now has to carry a first-time starter.

teams.name: New England Patriots
teams.headline: Pats reach Munich after 45-27 loss

stories.text: Patriots land in Munich after a 45-27 loss to Green Bay
stories.summary: New England fell to 5-4 after allowing 45 points, the most of Mike Vrabel's tenure. Drake Maye threw three interceptions and now leads the NFL with 11. The Patriots face the 6-2 Lions in Munich on Sunday, and a loss would make them 5-5.

stories.text: A.J. Brown practices again, Stevenson works off to the side
stories.summary: Brown, who missed two games with an ankle and knee issue, took part in his second straight practice in Munich. Running back Rhamondre Stevenson (knee) did not join stretching but worked on his own. Center Ben Brown (knee) is out, cornerback Carlton Davis III stayed home, and guard Walter Rouse is in the concussion protocol. The Friday report will say more.

stories.text: DeMario Douglas catches 5 for 102 against Green Bay
stories.summary: Douglas led the offense in a rough game with five catches and 102 yards. He played 42 snaps. With Brown back at practice, he said it feels good to have that leader back.

stories.text: -4: Patriots lose the turnover battle by four
stories.summary: New England forced no turnovers while Green Bay took the ball away four times. Cornerback Christian Gonzalez gave up 10 catches for 187 yards and a touchdown in coverage, a career high. The Patriots entered the week 11th in DVOA.

stories.text: Patriots face the Lions Sunday at 9:30 a.m. on FOX
stories.summary: The game is at FC Bayern's stadium in Munich, the last of the NFL's European games this year. Detroit averages 27.8 points per game. After Sunday the Patriots hit their bye, then meet Buffalo, Minnesota, Kansas City and Denver. Watch the makeshift offensive line against the Lions' pass rush.

teams.name: New York Jets
teams.headline: Jets host Bills on four-game skid

stories.text: Jets limp into Buffalo game on a four-game skid
stories.summary: New York is 2-7 after a 35-12 loss at Kansas City. The Jets host the 7-1 Bills on Sunday, their last home game before a two-game road trip and a bye. Andre Cisco went to Detroit for a 2029 sixth-round pick, the team's only deadline trade.

stories.text: Garrett Wilson still limited in concussion protocol
stories.summary: Wilson practiced on a limited basis Wednesday and Thursday after missing the Chiefs game. Coach Aaron Glenn said he is very hopeful Wilson plays. Defensive lineman Harrison Phillips (ankle) and linebacker Trevin Wallace (groin) did not practice Thursday. Receiver Omar Cooper Jr. (ankle) was limited. One earlier report called Wilson out, so watch for the official designation.

stories.text: Rookie David Bailey wrecks the Chiefs' protection
stories.summary: The rookie edge rusher had two sacks, two forced fumbles and nine tackles in the loss at Kansas City, the one bright spot on the day. Through eight career games he has 40 pressures along with those two sacks and two forced fumbles.

stories.text: 5: Jets have scored on their opening drive five straight games
stories.summary: That is the longest active streak in the NFL, according to the team. The fast starts have not turned into wins during a four-game losing streak. Geno Smith ranks fifth among qualified quarterbacks with a 67.5 completion percentage.

stories.text: Jets host the Bills Sunday at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: The game is at MetLife Stadium. Buffalo leads the NFL in yards and points per game, and Glenn says everything starts with Josh Allen. Watch whether Breece Hall, back from a five-game absence, can keep the ball away from that offense.

teams.name: Baltimore Ravens
teams.headline: Ravens skid to four straight, last in the North

stories.text: Jaguars run over the Ravens 33-10 on Thursday night
stories.summary: Jacksonville beat a depleted Baltimore team 33-10 in Week 9 and pushed the Ravens to 4-5. It was their fourth straight loss, and it left them last in the AFC North. Coach Jesse Minter declined to discuss Lamar Jackson's status after the game.

stories.text: Jackson's thumb injury leaves the Ravens thin at quarterback
stories.summary: Lamar Jackson lasted one play against Buffalo in Week 8 before hurting his right thumb, one game after he came back from a high ankle sprain. Minter said Jackson would have surgery and go on injured reserve, which means at least four missed games. Backup Tyler Huntley also got hurt in that game, and SI reported a turf toe injury that ends his season.

stories.text: Ryan Neuzil arrives to steady the middle of the line
stories.summary: Baltimore got the center from Atlanta at the Tuesday deadline for guard Andrew Vorhees and a reported conditional 2028 sixth-round pick. Neuzil started all 17 games for the Falcons last year, and his PFF grade ranks 15th among centers with at least half their team's snaps. He played for Dwayne Ledford in Atlanta, and Ledford now coaches the Ravens' line.

stories.text: 4: straight losses since a 4-1 start
stories.summary: The Ravens opened 4-1 and have lost four in a row since, falling to 4-5. The pass defense has finished above minus 1 percent DVOA only once this season, in Week 1, according to the BetMGM preview.

stories.text: Ravens host the Chargers on Monday night
stories.summary: Baltimore plays Los Angeles at M&T Bank Stadium on Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN. The Chargers were 0-8 entering the week, and this is a chance to stop the slide. Watch the quarterback decision and whether safety Kyle Hamilton and cornerback Nate Wiggins can play.

teams.name: Cincinnati Bengals
teams.headline: Bengals win in Madrid, Steelers next for first place

stories.text: Bengals beat the Falcons 34-17 in Madrid for a fourth straight win
stories.summary: Cincinnati took the franchise's first win outside the United States at Bernabeu Stadium on Sunday and moved to 6-2. Joe Burrow scored on a sneak and threw three touchdowns. The Bengals now sit one spot behind Pittsburgh in the AFC North and meet them Sunday night.

stories.text: No new injuries reported out of Madrid
stories.summary: Game coverage of the win over Atlanta listed no new Bengals injuries. A headline on the Bengals beat coverage points to encouraging news on guard Dylan Fairchild ahead of the Steelers game, but the article gave no details, so check the official Thursday and Friday reports.

stories.text: Ja'Marr Chase posts a 155-yard day in Madrid
stories.summary: Chase caught 10 passes for 155 yards and a 47-yard touchdown. He had 8 catches for 142 yards by halftime, the best first half by a Bengals player since 1988. Tee Higgins added two touchdowns.

stories.text: 24 of 29: Burrow's line in Madrid
stories.summary: Joe Burrow completed 24 of 29 passes for 271 yards, three touchdowns and no interceptions. He added a 1-yard rushing score, his third of the season. The running game gained 123 yards, 57 of them from Chase Brown.

stories.text: Steelers visit Paycor Stadium on Sunday night
stories.summary: Cincinnati hosts Pittsburgh on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Both teams are 6-2 and riding four-game winning streaks. The Steelers won the Week 3 meeting 30-27, so a Bengals win splits the series and gives them a one-game division lead.

teams.name: Cleveland Browns
teams.headline: Browns fall in OT at New Orleans, Texans visit

stories.text: Browns lose 23-22 in overtime at the Saints
stories.summary: Cleveland led 13-9 before New Orleans scored with 58 seconds left, and the Browns tied it with a field goal to force overtime. Harold Fannin Jr. answered the Saints' overtime touchdown with a 39-yard score, but the two-point try failed. The loss dropped Cleveland to 5-4.

stories.text: Watson and Collins both listed questionable for Texans
stories.summary: Deshaun Watson sat out the Saints game after he entered concussion protocol following a hit in the Steelers game, and Shedeur Sanders started in his place. Sports Illustrated lists Watson and defensive tackle Maliek Collins as questionable for Sunday. Cleveland's Nov. 10 depth chart still shows Watson as the starter.

stories.text: Carson Schwesinger piles up 14 tackles and two sacks
stories.summary: The linebacker also forced a fumble in the loss at New Orleans. Myles Garrett returned from injury with three sacks, and Myles Harden added two. The defense kept Cleveland in front for most of regulation.

stories.text: 7: straight field goals from 50-plus for Andre Szmyt
stories.summary: Szmyt hit a 51-yarder against the Saints, his seventh straight make from beyond 50 yards. The kick helped Cleveland tie the game late and force overtime.

stories.text: Texans visit Huntington Bank Field on Sunday
stories.summary: Cleveland hosts Houston on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on FOX. The Browns are 3-0 at home this season. The Texans are 3-5 and coming off a 44-22 win at the Chargers, in which C.J. Stroud threw for 384 yards and five touchdowns.

teams.name: Pittsburgh Steelers
teams.headline: Rested Steelers eye AFC North lead in Cincinnati

stories.text: Steelers come off the bye with the division lead on the line
stories.summary: Pittsburgh is 6-2 with four straight wins after beating the Browns 27-6 on Nov. 1. Coach Mike McCarthy said the team has a chance to sweep the Bengals. A win Sunday night gives the Steelers the head-to-head tiebreaker.

stories.text: Pittman nears a return from injured reserve
stories.summary: Receiver Michael Pittman Jr. has a plantar fascia injury and is eligible to return against the Bengals, though the Steelers had not opened his practice window as of Monday. McCarthy said he is getting close. Roman Wilson, also on injured reserve, becomes eligible after this game.

stories.text: Jaylen Warren is averaging 5.9 yards a carry
stories.summary: Warren has 704 rushing yards and seven rushing touchdowns through eight games. He gives the offense its steadiest production as Aaron Rodgers has 13 touchdowns and six interceptions on the year.

stories.text: 18.0: points allowed per game, fourth in the NFL
stories.summary: The Steelers also rank sixth in yards allowed and third against the run. T.J. Watt has 7.5 sacks and Jamel Dean has three forced fumbles.

stories.text: Steelers visit the Bengals on Sunday Night Football
stories.summary: Pittsburgh plays at Paycor Stadium on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 8:20 p.m. ET on NBC and Peacock. Both teams are 6-2 with four-game winning streaks. The Steelers won the Week 3 meeting 30-27 in Pittsburgh.

teams.name: Houston Texans
teams.headline: Texans ride a 44-22 rout to Cleveland

stories.text: Texans go to Cleveland with the wind at their backs
stories.summary: Houston opened 0-4 and has won three of its last four, the latest a 44-22 romp over the Chargers after the bye. Now the Texans visit a Browns team that is 3-0 at home and starts former Houston quarterback Deshaun Watson. Houston is a 4.5-point favorite.

stories.text: Montgomery still sidelined as Texans open the week
stories.summary: Running back David Montgomery (groin) did not practice Wednesday and has not played since Week 5. Linebacker Azeez Al-Shaair, tight end Brevin Jordan and guard Keylan Rutledge also sat out. Tank Dell, Marvin Harrison Jr. and safety Reed Blankenship (concussion) were limited.

stories.text: Boutte and Dell supply the deep shots in the rout
stories.summary: Kayshon Boutte set a career high with 125 receiving yards and two touchdowns against the Chargers, including a 63-yard score in the fourth quarter. Tank Dell returned from a knee injury that cost him almost two years and caught four passes for 105 yards. C.J. Stroud threw five touchdown passes in the win.

stories.text: 9.5: Will Anderson Jr.'s league-best sack total
stories.summary: Anderson leads the NFL with 9.5 sacks, and he faces a Browns line that has given up a league-high 38. Houston ranks fifth in the league with 21 team sacks.

stories.text: At Browns, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Houston plays at Huntington Bank Field against a Browns team that is 5-4 overall. Watch the Texans pass rush against Cleveland's protection and whether Watson, back from a concussion, can stay upright.

teams.name: Indianapolis Colts
teams.headline: Colts sell receivers, keep Taylor and Jones

stories.text: Colts dump two receivers at the deadline, keep Taylor
stories.summary: Indianapolis sent Josh Downs to Kansas City and Keenan Allen to San Francisco before Tuesday's deadline. The Colts also turned down offers for running back Jonathan Taylor, reportedly including a second-round pick, and held onto quarterback Daniel Jones.

stories.text: No timetable for Pierce's return from heel injury
stories.summary: Receiver Alec Pierce re-injured the same left heel that had surgery in the offseason, went on injured reserve after Week 2, and coach Shane Steichen would not set a return date. With Downs and Allen gone, Pierce is the receiver the Colts are waiting on.

stories.text: Taylor carries the Colts' ground game almost alone
stories.summary: Jonathan Taylor has 656 of the team's 1,037 rushing yards and 8 of its 11 rushing touchdowns. Against Dallas he managed 13 carries for 46 yards in the 27-23 loss.

stories.text: 500: yards the Colts defense allowed Dallas, again
stories.summary: Indianapolis gave up more than 500 yards to the Cowboys, the third time this season it has done that. The Colts have allowed more than six yards per play in five games.

stories.text: Vs. Dolphins, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: The Colts, losers of five straight, host a Miami team that is 1-7 at Lucas Oil Stadium. Jones is listed as the starter. Watch whether the defense stops giving up big plays.

teams.name: Jacksonville Jaguars
teams.headline: Jaguars go all in with a three-game division lead

stories.text: Jaguars pay up for Bates and Davis, hold a big lead
stories.summary: Jacksonville gave Atlanta a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth for safety Jessie Bates III. It sent Philadelphia a 2027 first and a 2029 second for tackle Jordan Davis, and added Davon Godchaux from New Orleans. The Jaguars lead the AFC South by three games.

stories.text: Tuten sits again as Jaguars manage the backfield
stories.summary: Running back Bhayshul Tuten (ankle/foot) missed practice Wednesday and Thursday. Receiver Jakobi Meyers and end Travon Walker were limited Thursday after sitting out Wednesday. Bates and Davis also did not practice, listed as rest.

stories.text: Parker Washington leads the offense in receiving
stories.summary: Washington has 493 receiving yards and five touchdowns this season, and he scored on a 50-yard play in the 33-10 win over Baltimore. Trevor Lawrence has 18 touchdown passes against 4 interceptions.

stories.text: +9: Jacksonville's league-best turnover margin
stories.summary: No team in the league has a better turnover differential than the Jaguars. Their offense also scores 28.6 points per game, fourth in the NFL.

stories.text: At Titans, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Jacksonville visits Nissan Stadium as a 10-point favorite and has beaten Tennessee four straight times. The rematch comes in Week 12. Watch whether the run game gets going and how the Jaguars use Bates and Davis.

teams.name: Tennessee Titans
teams.headline: Titans keep selling veterans, deal Hooker to Buffalo

stories.text: Titans send Hooker to Buffalo for a second-round pick
stories.summary: Safety Amani Hooker went to the Bills with five interceptions, tied for the league lead. Tennessee had already traded Jeffery Simmons to Chicago, and the Hooker deal continues the rebuild by adding more draft capital.

stories.text: Tate and Skoronski still out of practice
stories.summary: Rookie receiver Carnell Tate (shoulder), guard Peter Skoronski (hamstring), linebackers Cody Barton (concussion) and Anthony Hill Jr. (neck) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Running back Tyjae Spears (knee) moved up to limited on Thursday.

stories.text: Cam Ward posts a first 300-yard game
stories.summary: In the overtime loss at Cincinnati, Ward threw for a career-high 304 yards and two touchdowns on 26 of 40 passing. He also ran for a career-high 41 yards.

stories.text: 25:37: Tennessee's time of possession, last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Titans hold the ball for 25 minutes, 37 seconds per game, the lowest average in the league. They score 18.0 points per game, 28th, against Jacksonville's 28.6.

stories.text: Vs. Jaguars, Sunday 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: Tennessee returns from its bye to host Jacksonville at Nissan Stadium. Watch whether Ward can avoid turnovers and keep the Jaguars from running away early.

teams.name: Denver Broncos
teams.headline: Broncos at 7-2 and set a one-score record

stories.text: Broncos win 16th straight one-score game, an NFL record
stories.summary: Denver beat Carolina 26-21 in Week 9 and now owns the longest streak of one-score regular-season wins in league history. The Broncos sit at 7-2 with five straight wins and lead the AFC West. Defensive lineman Zach Allen said the team's best football is still ahead.

stories.text: Secondary thinned out heading into the bye
stories.summary: Safeties Talanoa Hufanga and Brandon Jones missed the Carolina game, and cornerback Riley Moss left it after 17 snaps. Receiver Jaylen Waddle exited with a concussion after 14 snaps. Sean Payton said RJ Harvey will be back shortly, and the bye gives all of them extra time.

stories.text: Nik Bonitto leads a Denver pass rush grading near the top
stories.summary: Bonitto owns a 90.7 PFF pass-rush grade, second among 109 qualifying edge rushers. He has 30 pressures and five sacks through nine games. Denver also added linebacker Daiyan Henley from the Chargers at the deadline.

stories.text: 29.7%: Denver's third-down rate ranks last in the NFL
stories.summary: The Broncos win close games without moving the chains on third down. They also allow 124.3 rushing yards per game, 23rd in the league. Bo Nix has cut his hits taken from about four per game to about two over the last three weeks.

stories.text: Broncos return from the bye to host the Raiders
stories.summary: Denver hosts Las Vegas on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS at Empower Field at Mile High. Watch whether Harvey returns and whether Jonah Coleman keeps the lead back role after his snap share climbed to 77%.

teams.name: Kansas City Chiefs
teams.headline: Chiefs add WR Josh Downs at the deadline

stories.text: Chiefs trade for Colts receiver Josh Downs
stories.summary: Kansas City sent 2027 fourth- and fifth-round picks to Indianapolis for Downs and a 2027 seventh-round pick. The deal came at Tuesday's trade deadline and deepens a receiver room that already includes Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy.

stories.text: Moore and Woods missed practice again before Atlanta
stories.summary: Right tackle Jaylon Moore (ankle) and defensive tackle Peter Woods (neck) did not practice Wednesday or Thursday. Running back Jaydn Ott (hamstring) was limited Thursday. Patrick Mahomes, Travis Kelce, Rashee Rice and Xavier Worthy all practiced fully.

stories.text: Kenneth Walker III reaches 1,000 scrimmage yards
stories.summary: Walker scored three touchdowns and gained 143 scrimmage yards in the 35-12 win over the Jets. He has 1,044 scrimmage yards and 11 scrimmage touchdowns, tied with Jahmyr Gibbs for the NFL lead. He is the first Chiefs player past 1,000 yards since Isiah Pacheco in 2023.

stories.text: 63%: Harrison Butker's field goal rate trails the league
stories.summary: Butker has missed a kick in every game but Week 1, and that rate is the worst among kickers on a roster. Andy Reid will keep him for Atlanta even though Kansas City signed Justin Tucker to the practice squad.

stories.text: Chiefs visit the Falcons in Week 10
stories.summary: Kansas City plays at Atlanta on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS at Mercedes-Benz Stadium. The Falcons are 3-6. Watch the offensive line if Moore stays out and the interior defensive line, which is down to three healthy tackles.

teams.name: Las Vegas Raiders
teams.headline: Rookie Mendoza gets first start after Cousins trade

stories.text: Raiders name Fernando Mendoza their starting quarterback
stories.summary: General manager John Spytek made the call Wednesday, a day after Las Vegas traded Kirk Cousins to Minnesota for a 2027 third-round pick. The No. 1 overall pick makes his first NFL start Sunday against Seattle. Spytek said Mendoza passed every test.

stories.text: Raiders list four players on the Week 10 report
stories.summary: Defensive tackle Thomas Booker (ankle) and guard Trey Zuhn (concussion) were limited both Wednesday and Thursday. Defensive tackle Folorunso Fatukasi (shoulder, elbow) moved from limited to full. Tight end Ian Thomas (ankle) practiced fully both days.

stories.text: Brock Bowers keeps setting tight end marks
stories.summary: Bowers caught seven passes for 111 yards and a touchdown in the 38-17 loss at San Francisco. He has 658 receiving yards and six touchdowns, both best among tight ends. He is also the fastest tight end to 2,500 career receiving yards, doing it in 36 games.

stories.text: 2.9: Raiders' yards per carry is the lowest in the NFL
stories.summary: Las Vegas ran 15 times for 24 yards against the 49ers and has not had a 100-yard rushing game in six weeks. The defense also gives up a league-high 151.2 rushing yards per game, so Mendoza gets little help from the ground game on either side.

stories.text: Raiders host Seahawks and their former offensive coordinator
stories.summary: Las Vegas hosts Seattle on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:05 p.m. ET (1:05 p.m. PT) on CBS at Allegiant Stadium. Seahawks QB Sam Darnold did not practice Wednesday or Thursday with ribs and quadriceps injuries. Raiders coach Klint Kubiak ran Seattle's offense for its Super Bowl title run.

teams.name: Los Angeles Chargers
teams.headline: Chargers fall to 0-8 after 44-22 loss to Houston

stories.text: Chargers sink to 0-8 with a 44-22 loss to Houston
stories.summary: The Chargers are the NFL's only winless team, and the Titans and Dolphins sit at 1-7. Houston posted 485 yards and 44 points, both season highs against Los Angeles. The Chargers have not started 0-8 since the 2020 Jets.

stories.text: McConkey and nine others sat out Thursday practice
stories.summary: Receiver Ladd McConkey (back) did not practice after sitting out the Houston game with back spasms. Defensive lineman Justin Eboigbe, receiver Brenen Thompson and safety Kendall Williamson also missed practice. Tight end David Njoku and linebacker Denzel Perryman were limited as they ramp up.

stories.text: Justin Herbert takes a career-high eight sacks
stories.summary: Herbert went 13 of 23 for 193 yards, one touchdown and one interception behind a line that gave up eight sacks. X-rays on his hand came back negative, and Jim Harbaugh said he is good to go. Herbert has thrown an interception in all eight games.

stories.text: 37: drives in a row without a touchdown ended in Houston
stories.summary: Herbert's 58-yard touchdown pass to Quentin Johnston finally snapped the streak early in the fourth quarter. Los Angeles scored three field goals on its first four drives against the Texans, then went scoreless on its next six.

stories.text: Chargers visit Ravens on Monday night
stories.summary: Los Angeles plays at Baltimore on Monday, Nov. 16 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at M&T Bank Stadium. It is the Harbaugh brothers matchup, and the Ravens have won the last three meetings. Watch Herbert's protection and McConkey's back.

teams.name: Dallas Cowboys
teams.headline: Cowboys escape Indy, then face a thin 49ers week

stories.text: Cowboys steal one in Indianapolis, 27-23
stories.summary: Dallas blew a 17-7 halftime lead and still beat the Colts. Dak Prescott led a four-play, 65-yard touchdown drive that took 29 seconds, and Javonte Williams punched in the winning score from the 1. The Cowboys sit at 4-5 and host San Francisco next.

stories.text: Locke out again, Ferguson and Goodson down for weeks
stories.summary: Safety P.J. Locke is out after what looked like another concussion. Tight end Jake Ferguson and running back Tyler Goodson both have knee injuries and should miss multiple weeks. George Pickens (hamstring) and Joey Porter Jr. moved from out to questionable, and Donovan Ezeiruaku has an ankle sprain with his status open. Statuses are from Monday's update, so check the final Friday designations.

stories.text: CeeDee Lamb piles up 195 yards in Indy
stories.summary: Lamb caught 10 passes for 195 yards and a touchdown against the Colts. He did it with Pickens ruled out 90 minutes before kickoff. Prescott finished 21 of 34 for 335 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: 508: Cowboys total yards in the win over Indianapolis
stories.summary: Dallas gained 508 yards against the Colts and still needed a last-minute drive to win. The offense also took 14 penalties for 153 yards, a flag count that kept the Colts in it. The Cowboys have scored 230 points and allowed 230 through nine games.

stories.text: 49ers at AT&T Stadium, Sunday on FOX
stories.summary: Dallas hosts San Francisco (7-1) on Sunday, Nov. 15 at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX. The Niners lead the NFC West and average 6.2 yards per play. Watch Dallas on third down, where it has converted 45.3 percent, and the penalty count.

teams.name: New York Giants
teams.headline: Giants blow late lead, lose to Washington 24-21

stories.text: Giants lose on Diggs' 32-yard touchdown with 57 seconds left
stories.summary: New York led 21-17 after a 66-yard Isaiah Likely touchdown, then watched Jayden Daniels drive Washington down the field for the winner. J.J. McCarthy threw for 293 yards but an interception with 25 seconds left sealed it. The Giants drop to 5-3-1 and keep a two-game lead in the NFC East.

stories.text: McCarthy and Skattebo play through hip and hamstring issues
stories.summary: McCarthy hurt his hip against the Eagles when Zack Baun hit him, and Cam Skattebo missed that game with a hamstring injury. Both were limited early in the week and both played Thursday. Linebacker Malik Harrison (groin) was the only Giant on the final injury report, listed questionable.

stories.text: Isaiah Likely goes for 127 yards on nine catches
stories.summary: Likely caught nine passes for 127 yards and a touchdown against Washington, including the 66-yard score that gave New York the lead. Skattebo ran 18 times for 78 yards and two touchdowns and added 44 receiving yards.

stories.text: 0-4-1: Giants' record against Jayden Daniels
stories.summary: Daniels has beaten the Giants three times and tied them once in four starts. The teams also played to a 27-27 overtime tie in Week 5. The Giants still hold a two-game division lead, but Washington owns the tiebreaker.

stories.text: Jaguars at MetLife, Sunday Nov. 22 on CBS
stories.summary: The Giants host Jacksonville (6-2) on Sunday, Nov. 22 at 4:25 p.m. ET on CBS. The league moved the game from 1 p.m. Watch how New York bounces back from a loss it led late, and whether the defense holds up against a team with a better record.

teams.name: Philadelphia Eagles
teams.headline: Eagles hit the bye on a seven-game skid

stories.text: Eagles enter the bye with seven straight losses
stories.summary: Philadelphia is 2-7, and its last win came Sept. 20 at Tennessee. It is the longest skid since an eight-game slide in 2012. Playoff odds sit at 0.2 percent, and Nick Sirianni did not rule out staff changes during the bye.

stories.text: Hurts stays on IR as backs and receivers keep falling
stories.summary: Jalen Hurts went on injured reserve Oct. 17 with blood clots in his lungs and is expected to miss the rest of the season. Saquon Barkley has missed time with several injuries, and Dontayvion Wicks missed games with an ankle injury. Tank Bigsby, Will Shipley, Carson Steele and Dameon Pierce have all been lost at running back this year. The team is off this week.

stories.text: Jalen Carter has 5 sacks and 4 forced fumbles
stories.summary: The defensive tackle has 5 sacks, 4 forced fumbles, 7 tackles for loss and 25 tackles through nine games. Linebacker Zack Baun leads the team with 65 tackles and has 5 pass breakups. Carter has been solid, though not consistently elite, according to one midterm review.

stories.text: 126-40: Eagles' second-half scoring deficit this season
stories.summary: Opponents have outscored Philadelphia 126-40 after halftime. The Eagles have not topped 341 total yards in any game, and Barkley averages 42.3 rushing yards per game. The offense scores 16.4 points per game, 30th in the NFL.

stories.text: Bye week, then Steelers on Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. on CBS
stories.summary: Philadelphia is off in Week 10. It returns home Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET on CBS against Pittsburgh (6-2). Watch the quarterback spot, where Tanner McKee and Joe Milton III have both started since Hurts went down.

teams.name: Washington Commanders
teams.headline: Daniels' late drive beats Giants, keeps hopes alive

stories.text: Daniels drives Washington 71 yards in 49 seconds to beat Giants
stories.summary: Jayden Daniels threw a 32-yard touchdown to Stefon Diggs for the go-ahead score in a 24-21 win Thursday night. It came right after his first two interceptions of the season, which came on back-to-back fourth-quarter drives. Washington is 3-5-1, two games behind New York, and owns the tiebreaker.

stories.text: Patrick and Yankoff were out for Thursday's game
stories.summary: Center Lucas Patrick (concussion) and tight end Colson Yankoff (knee) were ruled out for the Giants game. No new injuries were reported from the win. Washington's next injury report comes ahead of the Nov. 23 game against Cincinnati.

stories.text: Diggs catches the winner, Daniels throws three scores
stories.summary: Daniels went 23 of 33 for 249 yards and three touchdowns with two interceptions. Diggs finished with six catches for 83 yards, including the 32-yard winner. Ben Sinnott had four catches for 42 yards and a touchdown after entering with one reception all season.

stories.text: 7-17-1: Washington's record since the start of last season
stories.summary: That is where Dan Quinn's team stood before Thursday's win, per ESPN. The Commanders now have forced six turnovers in their last three games. Rasul Douglas ended New York's last drive with an interception.

stories.text: Bengals visit Monday night, Nov. 23 on ESPN
stories.summary: Washington hosts Cincinnati on Monday, Nov. 23 at 8:15 p.m. ET on ESPN at Northwest Stadium. The Commanders get 11 days between games. Watch whether the offense protects Daniels again, after he was sacked only once against New York.

teams.name: Chicago Bears
teams.headline: Bears hit the bye on a four-game win streak

stories.text: Bears survive four picks and head into the bye at 7-2
stories.summary: Chicago beat Tampa Bay 27-24 on Sunday after Caleb Williams threw a career-high four interceptions, one more than he had thrown all season. Tampa Bay tied it at 24 with 2:51 left, and Cairo Santos won it with a 38-yard field goal as time expired. The Bears have won four straight and now rest in Week 10.

stories.text: Monangai nears a return from a toe injury
stories.summary: Running back Kyle Monangai practiced for the first time in over a month on Friday after hurting his toe in Week 4. The Bears are using the bye to give him two more weeks before the Saints game. Cornerbacks Tyrique Stevenson (thumb) and Malik Muhammad (toe) played through questionable tags last week, and tackle Theo Benedet was cleared after a shoulder scare against Seattle.

stories.text: Jaylon Johnson's 67-yard pick-six keeps the Bears alive
stories.summary: Johnson took an interception 67 yards for a touchdown against Tampa Bay, one of the few clean plays in a sloppy win. Tight end Colston Loveland then caught a 38-yard pass on the winning drive to set up Santos. Williams finished with 279 yards and two touchdowns.

stories.text: 2 of 12: Tampa Bay's third-down conversions against Chicago
stories.summary: The Bucs converted only two of 12 third downs, and that is a big reason the Bears survived five turnovers. Chicago scored just three points over a 10-drive stretch and still held on. Fixing the giveaways is the work for the bye.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then the Saints at home
stories.summary: Chicago is off this Sunday. The first game back is against New Orleans on Sunday, Nov. 22 at home, followed by a Thanksgiving trip to Detroit in Week 12. Watch whether Monangai is back and how Williams cleans up the turnovers.

teams.name: Detroit Lions
teams.headline: Lions fly to Munich on a four-game win streak

stories.text: Lions grind out a 19-9 win in Miami to reach 6-2
stories.summary: Detroit won its fourth straight on Sunday behind Jahmyr Gibbs' 8-yard touchdown and four field goals from Jake Bates. The offense was quiet, but the defense held Miami to nine points. The Lions now travel to Munich for a Week 10 game with New England.

stories.text: Mays, Reed and Joseph out for the Germany game
stories.summary: Center Cade Mays (ankle), cornerback D.J. Reed (hip) and safety Kerby Joseph (knee) are ruled out against New England. Quarterback Jared Goff (chest) and edge DJ Wonnum (concussion) were full participants, and receiver Amon-Ra St. Brown (rib) was limited. Running back Sione Vaki (ankle) did not practice but is traveling with the team.

stories.text: Jake Bates goes 4 for 4 as the offense stalls
stories.summary: Bates hit field goals from 28, 33, 40 and 43 yards and supplied most of Detroit's points in Miami. Gibbs added 20 carries for 74 yards and his 11th touchdown from scrimmage this season. Goff finished 17 of 25 for 170 yards with three sacks and a tipped interception.

stories.text: 30th: Where Detroit's defense ranks in opponent EPA per play
stories.summary: Despite the win in Miami, the Lions rank 30th in opponent EPA per play and 21st in opponent yards per play at 5.4. Detroit also lost All-Pro linebacker Jack Campbell to injured reserve with a neck injury suffered against Minnesota on Nov. 1. Drake Maye, who ranks fifth in adjusted EPA per play, is next.

stories.text: Patriots in Munich, Sunday at 9:30 a.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Detroit (6-2) plays New England (5-4) at the home of FC Bayern Munich in the NFL's Germany game. The Patriots lost cornerback Carlton Davis III and guard Ben Brown to ruled-out designations, so watch how the Lions' short-handed secondary handles Maye.

teams.name: Green Bay Packers
teams.headline: Packers face Vikings without their top back

stories.text: Love throws for 372 yards as Packers rout Patriots 45-27
stories.summary: Jordan Love threw for 372 yards and three touchdowns and ran for another score on Sunday in Foxborough. Green Bay forced four turnovers and finished with 478 total yards. The 6-3 Packers now host Minnesota at Lambeau Field.

stories.text: Jacobs fractured a finger and needs surgery
stories.summary: Josh Jacobs broke the ring finger on his right hand in the first quarter against New England and needs surgery. Coach Matt LaFleur did not rule out injured reserve, which means at least four games. MarShawn Lloyd is out with a knee injury, so Kaleb Johnson and Pierre Strong Jr. handle the backfield.

stories.text: Watson and Golden both top 160 yards in New England
stories.summary: Christian Watson caught seven passes for 171 yards and a touchdown, and Matthew Golden caught 10 for 164 and a score. Safety Xavier McKinney intercepted Drake Maye twice. The pair gave Love two reliable targets all afternoon.

stories.text: Last: Where Green Bay's rushing offense ranks in the NFL
stories.summary: The Packers rank last in rushing offense even after a 6-3 start. Jacobs has 36 carries for 80 yards (2.2 per carry) since he returned from the commissioner exempt list, where he sat for the first six games. His absence leaves a thin backfield for the Vikings game.

stories.text: Vikings at Lambeau, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: Minnesota visits Green Bay in a Week 10 NFC North game, and the Vikings may start Kirk Cousins, who tore his Achilles at Lambeau in 2023. Green Bay then has its bye in Week 11 before a trip to the Rams in Week 12. Watch how the Packers move the ball on the ground without Jacobs.

teams.name: Minnesota Vikings
teams.headline: Vikings trade for Cousins after a prime-time flop

stories.text: Vikings reacquire Kirk Cousins for a 2027 third-round pick
stories.summary: Minnesota sent a third-round pick to Las Vegas for Cousins on deadline day. Coach Kevin O'Connell would not promise a start Sunday and said the plan is to make sure Cousins feels comfortable in the offense. New general manager Nolan Teasley said the trade had been discussed for weeks and was not a reaction to Carson Wentz's bad night.

stories.text: Murray still sidelined with a hamstring strain
stories.summary: Kyler Murray strained his hamstring on a read-option run at Detroit on Nov. 1 and missed the Buffalo game. O'Connell said the team wants to avoid making it worse, and Murray was not ready to practice this week. Wentz was checked for a lower leg injury on Monday night, and Max Brosmer finished the game.

stories.text: Jefferson draws 11 targets and catches three
stories.summary: Justin Jefferson caught three passes for 58 yards on 11 targets in the 23-6 loss to Buffalo. Wentz went 8 of 25 for 81 yards with three turnovers, and Minnesota gained 178 yards. Cousins was second in the league with 20 touchdown passes for Las Vegas this season.

stories.text: 178: Total yards for Minnesota in the loss to Buffalo
stories.summary: The Vikings never crossed the Bills' 48-yard line in the first half and managed 178 yards on Monday night. Their defense still sacked Josh Allen four times. O'Connell said afterward, "Put tonight 100% on me."

stories.text: At Green Bay, Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on Fox
stories.summary: The Vikings (6-2) visit the Packers (6-3) at Lambeau Field. Cousins is the likely starter, but O'Connell has not committed to it. Watch for how quickly the offense learns to protect him against a Green Bay pass rush.

teams.name: Atlanta Falcons
teams.headline: Falcons sell Bates and Neuzil, host Chiefs

stories.text: Falcons trade safety Jessie Bates III to Jacksonville
stories.summary: Atlanta sent Bates to the Jaguars on Monday for a 2027 second-round pick and a 2028 fifth-rounder. He had a career-high 14 tackles in Sunday's loss to Cincinnati and was in the last year of his contract. Coach Kevin Stefanski said the team has not given up on 2026 and named DeMarcco Hellams the next man up at safety. The Falcons also moved center Ryan Neuzil to Baltimore for guard Andrew Vorhees and a 2028 sixth-rounder.

stories.text: Pearce and Dexter return to limited practice
stories.summary: Edge James Pearce Jr. (back) and tackle Gervon Dexter Sr. (illness) practiced on a limited basis Thursday, though neither is fully cleared for Sunday. Receiver Zachariah Branch (hamstring) and linebacker Divine Deablo (forearm) did not practice. Cam Thomas (groin), Kendal Daniels (Achilles) and Josh Woods (ankle) were limited. Stefanski said Pearce, back from an eight-game suspension, still needs to regain strength and shake off rust.

stories.text: Bijan Robinson posts first 100-yard game of 2026
stories.summary: Robinson ran 19 times for 100 yards and a touchdown against the Bengals in Madrid, his first 100-yard game this season. He also led Atlanta with six catches for 47 yards. The Falcons still lost 34-17 and fell to 3-6. Kansas City comes to town next, and Robinson will test a Chiefs run defense that has allowed just over 96 rushing yards per game.

stories.text: 12: Falcons penalties, a season high, in Madrid
stories.summary: Atlanta drew 12 flags for 88 yards against Cincinnati, and many came before the snap. Left guard Matthew Bergeron and right tackle Jawaan Taylor each jumped, and a Taylor holding call erased a first down. Stefanski called the mistakes self-inflicted and inexcusable and made fixing them the week's top job.

stories.text: Chiefs visit Atlanta on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET
stories.summary: Kansas City (6-2) plays at Mercedes-Benz Stadium on CBS. The Falcons have lost two straight and recently swapped kicker Nick Folk for Jake Moody. Bates and Neuzil are gone, so watch the safety spot and Corey Levin, the likely starter at center. Patrick Mahomes is expected to play after an elbow scare.

teams.name: Carolina Panthers
teams.headline: Panthers chase first place in New Orleans

stories.text: Panthers and Saints meet for first place at 3-5
stories.summary: Carolina has lost three straight but sits tied atop the NFC South because every team in the division is under .500. The Panthers made no trades at the deadline, the second year in a row for GM Dan Morgan. Coach Dave Canales fired defensive coordinator Ejiro Evero on Oct. 30 and promoted Todd Wash. A win Sunday gives Carolina sole possession of first.

stories.text: Reinforcements back at practice, Okereke sits
stories.summary: Running back Jonathon Brooks (groin), cornerback Mike Jackson (groin), receiver Xavier Legette (knee) and guard Brady Christensen (hamstring) all practiced fully Thursday after opening their practice windows from injured reserve. Linebacker Bobby Okereke (foot) did not practice for a second day. Edge Jaelan Phillips (hamstring) and guard Damien Lewis (knee) were limited.

stories.text: Bryce Young throws for three scores in loss
stories.summary: Young went 28 of 39 for 276 yards and three touchdowns against Denver, with a 106.4 passer rating. Darren Waller caught eight passes for 90 yards and a score, and Tetairoa McMillan added a touchdown. Nik Bonitto's strip-sack with 1:24 left sealed the 26-21 loss.

stories.text: 13: Panthers penalties against Denver for 119 yards
stories.summary: Carolina tied for the third most penalties in team history, and Denver earned six first downs by penalty, matching the team record for most allowed that way. Five of the defense's seven flags were for pass interference, with the top four cornerbacks out hurt.

stories.text: Panthers at Saints on Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The game is at the Caesars Superdome, with first place in the division on the line. Carolina has to protect Young against a Saints front led by Chase Young, who has eight sacks, and Carl Granderson, who has 7.5. Watch how the secondary holds up with Will Lee III and Mike Jackson back at practice.

teams.name: New Orleans Saints
teams.headline: Saints host Panthers with first place at stake

stories.text: Saints beat Browns in overtime, eye first place
stories.summary: Tyler Shough led an 11-play, 74-yard overtime drive, and New Orleans beat Cleveland 23-22 for its first home win of 2026. The defense stopped a two-point try on the final play. The Saints, now 3-5, share the NFC South lead with Carolina and have won two of their last three. They also traded defensive tackle Davon Godchaux to Jacksonville.

stories.text: Center Erik McCoy out, Etienne closer to return
stories.summary: McCoy (biceps) will not play, so Cesar Ruiz slides to center and rookie Jeremiah Wright starts at right guard. Running back Travis Etienne Jr. (hamstring), on injured reserve, practiced on a limited basis and could play for the first time in six games. Alvin Kamara was a full participant Thursday. Tackle Kelvin Banks Jr. (ankle) and cornerback Martin Emerson Jr. (shin) were limited.

stories.text: Carl Granderson keeps piling up multi-sack games
stories.summary: Granderson had two sacks against Cleveland, his fourth straight game with multiple sacks. The team says he is the first NFL player to do that since 2013. He has 7.5 sacks this season, one behind teammate Chase Young, who has eight.

stories.text: 2020: last Saints overtime win before the Browns game
stories.summary: The 23-22 win over Cleveland was New Orleans' first overtime victory since 2020 and moved its all-time overtime record to 16-16. The Saints outrushed the Browns 160-95 and sacked them five times.

stories.text: Panthers visit the Superdome Sunday at 1 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The winner takes sole possession of first place in the NFC South. The Saints won both meetings last season, 17-7 in Carolina and 20-17 at home. Watch the interior line without McCoy and whether Etienne returns to the backfield.

teams.name: Tampa Bay Buccaneers
teams.headline: Bucs use bye to fix run-heavy offense

stories.text: Bucs hit the bye 3-6 and half a game back
stories.summary: Tampa Bay lost 27-24 in Chicago on a last-second field goal and trails the Saints and Panthers by half a game. Coach Todd Bowles said the staff will cut Bucky Irving's carries and use the bye to review the passing game under Baker Mayfield. Kenny Gainwell is the likely partner in the backfield.

stories.text: Antoine Winfield Jr. left Chicago game with ankle injury
stories.summary: The safety went down in the first half Sunday night and did not return. No severity has been reported, and Tampa Bay is off this week. Receiver Emeka Egbuka returned from a two-game foot absence and caught three passes for 38 yards. Ifeatu Melifonwu filled in for Winfield.

stories.text: Zyon McCollum picks off Caleb Williams twice
stories.summary: McCollum has an interception in three straight games and leads the team with four this season. He had two against Chicago. Safety Tykee Smith and linebacker Alex Anzalone also intercepted Williams, and Anzalone's fourth pick is the most by a front-seven player in the league.

stories.text: 22: straight wins ended when Bucs force five turnovers
stories.summary: Tampa Bay had won 22 straight games when it forced five takeaways before Chicago beat it 27-24. The Bucs scored off only two of them. Mayfield's pick-six, returned 67 yards by Jaylon Johnson, was the difference, and the offense went 2 for 12 on third down.

stories.text: Bye in Week 10, then at the Lions Nov. 22
stories.summary: Tampa Bay returns Sunday, Nov. 22 at 1 p.m. ET at Ford Field on FOX against Detroit (6-2). Watch how the Bucs handle Jahmyr Gibbs, who leads the league in scrimmage yards with 1,132, and whether Irving's workload shrinks.

teams.name: Arizona Cardinals
teams.headline: Rookie Carson Beck gets the keys against the Rams

stories.text: Minshew lands on IR, and Arizona rebuilds its quarterback room
stories.summary: The Cardinals put Gardner Minshew on injured reserve Tuesday after Dante Fowler Jr. hit his throwing arm on the last play of the first half in Seattle. Minshew finished that game anyway, but he is not expected back this season. Arizona signed 40-year-old Josh Johnson off the Bengals practice squad, his 15th NFL team, a week after shipping Jacoby Brissett to Baltimore.

stories.text: Froholdt in concussion protocol as five starters sit Wednesday
stories.summary: Lineman Hjalte Froholdt (concussion), lineman Jon Gaines II (ankle) and defensive lineman Roy Lopez (toe, ankle) missed Wednesday's practice. Budda Baker, Isaac Seumalo, Josh Sweat and Mack Wilson Sr. also sat, mostly for rest. Running back Bam Knight (concussion) and cornerback Max Melton (knee, hand) were limited, and the team has Zach Carter and Hunter Long practicing in their IR return windows.

stories.text: Carson Beck goes from emergency QB to Sunday starter
stories.summary: Beck, a third-round rookie, spent the first eight weeks as the emergency third quarterback and sat inactive on game days. He played 55 college games at Georgia and Miami, and his last snap came in the national title game loss to Indiana in January. Coach Mike LaFleur says Beck will not shy away from throwing deep, though Arizona's active receivers have just eight catches combined this season.

stories.text: 11: straight losses to Seattle after Sunday's 17-3 defeat
stories.summary: Arizona has dropped 11 in a row to the Seahawks after managing just 198 total yards at Lumen Field. The offense went 4 of 13 on third down and put together eight straight scoreless drives after a first-quarter Chad Ryland field goal. The loss dropped the Cardinals to 3-6.

stories.text: Rams visit State Farm Stadium Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS
stories.summary: Beck makes his first career start against a Rams team that has won three straight. Watch how he handles a pass rush led by Myles Garrett, who had three sacks in his return last week. Trey McBride led Arizona with seven catches in Seattle and should see plenty of targets again.

teams.name: Los Angeles Rams
teams.headline: Rams reverse course and put Puka Nacua on IR

stories.text: Rams flip their call and place Puka Nacua on injured reserve
stories.summary: Sean McVay said Wednesday that Nacua would stay off IR for roster reasons, but the Rams moved him there anyway a day later. Nacua will miss Arizona, Green Bay, Kansas City and San Francisco, and he can return no earlier than the Dec. 20 home game against Dallas. Los Angeles elevated Brennan Presley from the practice squad and signed Tyler Scott to it.

stories.text: Avila, Curl and McDuffie sit out as Stafford practices fully
stories.summary: Guard Steve Avila (hamstring), safety Kam Curl (toe), cornerback Trent McDuffie (back) and tight end Terrance Ferguson (ankle, hamstring) did not practice Wednesday, and Nacua is out. Myles Garrett (knee), Davis Allen (oblique), Colby Parkinson (ribs) and long snapper Joe Cardona (ankle) were limited. Matthew Stafford was a full participant with his right elbow on the report.

stories.text: Myles Garrett wrecks Washington in his first game back
stories.summary: Garrett returned from knee surgery and posted three sacks, three quarterback hits and three tackles for loss in the 20-13 win at Washington. His strip sack late in the first half, recovered by Omar Speights, was his first sack as a Ram. He was limited in practice Wednesday with the same knee.

stories.text: 14: catches for Nacua on 19 targets in his last game before IR
stories.summary: Nacua turned those catches into 150 yards and the go-ahead score, a leaping 7-yard grab that broke a 13-13 tie in the fourth quarter. The win was the Rams' third straight and pushed them above .500 for the first time this season at 5-4. Stafford went 26 of 43 for 219 yards with one interception.

stories.text: At Arizona Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, then the bye
stories.summary: The Rams try to stretch their streak to four games before an open date in Week 11. Nacua and Davante Adams both sit, and tight end Terrance Ferguson pulled a hamstring in practice. The defense gets a rookie quarterback making his first start.

teams.name: San Francisco 49ers
teams.headline: 49ers add Keenan Allen and ride a 7-1 start to Dallas

stories.text: 49ers land Keenan Allen from Indianapolis for a sixth-round pick
stories.summary: San Francisco sent a 2027 sixth-rounder to the Colts for Allen less than an hour before Tuesday's trade deadline. Allen had 40 catches for 351 yards and one touchdown in eight games with Indianapolis, and his 1,095 career receptions rank eighth in league history. It is the second deal between the two clubs this season after the DeForest Buckner trade.

stories.text: Shanahan says Mike Evans is getting real close
stories.summary: Evans has missed two games with Achilles tendinitis and has not practiced since leaving the Week 6 win over Washington. Cornerbacks Renardo Green (back) and Deommodore Lenoir (foot) sat a second straight day Thursday, and Kyle Shanahan said they can still play without a Friday practice. Rookie defensive tackle Gracen Halton is done for the year with a fractured ankle.

stories.text: Brock Purdy throws his 100th career touchdown pass
stories.summary: Purdy reached the milestone in Sunday's 38-17 win over the Raiders, throwing for 232 yards and two scores and running for another. He also threw one interception. The 49ers never punted and ran for 190 yards on 43 carries, with Christian McCaffrey scoring twice.

stories.text: 5: second-half takeaways by the 49ers against Las Vegas
stories.summary: Jaden Dugger opened the second half with a 35-yard interception return for a touchdown, and Fred Warner forced one fumble and recovered another. San Francisco had not forced five takeaways against the Raiders since a game at Candlestick Park two decades ago. The win lifted the 49ers to 7-1.

stories.text: At Dallas Sunday at 4:25 p.m. ET on FOX
stories.summary: The 49ers take a 7-1 record into AT&T Stadium against the 4-5 Cowboys. Deebo Samuel returned to practice Wednesday after missing three games with a hamstring strain and expects to play, and Allen got his first practice in red and gold. Watch whether Green and Lenoir clear in time to face George Pickens.

teams.name: Seattle Seahawks
teams.headline: Drew Lock starts again as Darnold sits in Las Vegas

stories.text: Darnold ruled out again, so Drew Lock starts against the Raiders
stories.summary: Mike Macdonald ruled out Sam Darnold for Sunday as he recovers from quad and rib injuries, his third missed game this season. Lock will make another start despite elbow and oblique injuries, after a Monday exam that Macdonald called good. Lock went 19 of 28 for 175 yards and a touchdown in last week's 17-3 win over Arizona.

stories.text: Darnold and Quenton Nelson out, Charles Cross back to limited
stories.summary: Darnold and guard Quenton Nelson (knee) will not play in Las Vegas. Left tackle Charles Cross (ankle) moved from no practice Wednesday to limited Thursday, while defensive tackle Leonard Williams (stinger) sat both days, and Seattle has not decided on either. Lock, Derick Hall, Uchenna Nwosu and Anthony Bradford were limited both days, and Rashid Shaheed (knee) practiced fully.

stories.text: AJ Barner scores twice as Seattle smothers Arizona
stories.summary: The tight end scored on a 1-yard dive and caught a 7-yard touchdown from Lock, both in the second quarter of the 17-3 win. That made him the first Seahawk since Chris Carson in 2019 to score rushing and receiving touchdowns in the same quarter. Barner came off the injury report Thursday after a finger issue.

stories.text: 1,036: receiving yards for Jaxon Smith-Njigba through nine games
stories.summary: Smith-Njigba crossed 1,000 yards with seven catches for 51 yards against Arizona. He joins Tyler Lockett and Steve Largent as the only Seahawks with 1,000 receiving yards in three straight seasons. The win also gave Seattle 11 straight victories over the Cardinals, the longest streak against one opponent in team history.

stories.text: At Las Vegas Sunday at 4:05 p.m. ET on CBS, then the bye
stories.summary: Seattle heads to Las Vegas with Lock under center and an open date waiting in Week 11. Keep an eye on the left side of the line with Nelson out and Cross a game-time call. Lock has started twice this season, in Weeks 2 and 9.
